subject: Materials Science
title: Ionic and Covalent Bonds in Ceramics
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ionic and Covalent Bonds in Ceramics.

hook.text: Metals bend because their bonds are flexible. Ceramics crack because theirs are rigid.

buildup.text: Ionic bonds transfer electrons between atoms — strong but directional and brittle.

discovery.text: Covalent bonds share electrons tightly — even stronger but zero tolerance for misalignment.

twist.text: Most ceramics use both bond types, combining extreme hardness with zero ductility.

climax.text: Diamond is pure covalent bonding — the hardest material, yet it shatters on impact.

punchline.text: The strongest bonds make the most fragile materials.

quiz.question: Why are ceramics brittle despite strong bonds?
options: Their bonds are too weak to hold together
Their rigid bonds can't accommodate deformation
They contain too many free electrons
